tools.name: get_me
tools.description: Get the Cal.com profile this API key belongs to (username, email, timezone, organization)

tools.name: list_event_types
tools.description: List Cal.com event types, optionally filtered to one username or event slug

username.description: Optional Cal.com username to list event types for

event_slug.description: Optional event type slug to filter by (needs username)

tools.name: list_bookings
tools.description: List Cal.com bookings, optionally filtered by status or attendee email (cursor paginated)

status.description: Optional single status filter; omit to walk all statuses

attendee_email.description: Optional attendee email address to filter by

cursor.description: Optional opaque cursor from a previous response's next_cursor

needs_review: Tools written 2026-09-12 from Cal.com's own OpenAPI document (https://cal.com/docs/api-reference/v2/openapi.json, operationIds MeController_getMe, EventTypesController_2026_06_12_getEventTypes, BookingsController_2026_05_01_getBookings): GET /v2/me, GET /v2/event-types and GET /v2/bookings. All three are GET reads, write:false, and nothing that mutates a booking is expressed here.

base_url changed from the scaffolded https://api.cal.com to https://api.cal.com/v2 because v1 is gone. Observed live 2026-09-12: a GET outside /v2 on that host answers 410 with {"message":"API v1 has been decommissioned. Please migrate to API v2: https://cal.com/docs/api-reference/v2"}. Folding /v2 into base_url also puts the harness control probe under /v2, where the API answers a routed 404 NotFoundException, which is the differential the tool probes are read against.

Scaffolded auth kept (bearer on api_key) on documentary plus live evidence. The introduction page states verbatim "Authentication to the API is performed via the Authorization header" with `'Authorization': 'Bearer YOUR_API_KEY'`, and the OpenAPI Authorization parameter on /v2/me reads verbatim "value must be `Bearer <token>` where `<token>` is api key prefixed with cal_, managed user access token, or OAuth access token". The vault type collects exactly one field, api_key, with prefix cal_. No apiKey query parameter: that was the decommissioned v1 form.

cal-api-version is a REQUIRED header whose value is per-endpoint (OpenAPI: /v2/event-types requires 2026-06-12, /v2/bookings requires 2026-05-01, /v2/me takes no version), so it rides in per-tool request.headers, not static_headers. The shape-proof harness only sends static_headers, so those two probes reached the API WITHOUT the version header and were answered with a structured 403 ("PermissionsGuard - no oAuth client found for access token"); with the header the same call answers 401 ("Invalid Access Token."). Either way host, TLS, route and auth enforcement are proven; the version header's own effect is documented, NOT proven by this run.

list_bookings pages the 2026-05-01 way: `cursor` plus `limit` (OpenAPI minimum 1, maximum 100, default 50), clamped here to 20..100. The older 2024-08-13 take/skip pagination is deliberately not used, because the current reference says verbatim "Must pass `cal-api-version: 2026-05-01` header." for this endpoint. `status` filters to a single value per the same doc; parallel requests per status are the documented way to span several.

No _probe hints: none of these routes carries a tenant slug or an account prefix, so the harness's generic dummy inputs already route. Cal.com's documented API-key rate limit is 120 requests per minute; this spec declares the wave standard 30 per 60s, which is stricter.
